task.title: Creating a direct node connection
task.shortdesc: The node switch can accept and initiate direct connections with other BACnet/SC nodes. This procedure demonstrates how to connect two nodes, as an example, Node 1 and Node 2.

taskbody.prereq: The nodes have been enabled and configured. The bacnet palette is open.
taskbody.context: Secure Connect supports only secure web sockets.

step.cmd: To create a connection from Node 2 to Node 1, expand Node 2, expand LinkNode Switch and do one of the following:

choices.choice: Right-click Connections and choose ActionsAdd Connection. an Add Connection window opens.

In the palette, expand SecureConnect, drag an InitaingConnection1 component from the palette to the Connections folder under Node Switch and double-click InitiatingConnector1 in the Nav tree. The Direct Initiating Connection Property Sheet opens.

step.cmd: Configure the following connection properties and click OK or Save.

li.p: Connection Name provides a name for the connection.
Address or Peer Uri Address is the station address (Universal Resource Identifier), for example, Localhost.
Path or Peer Uri Path identifies the Node Switch path.

step.stepresult: This adds a New Initiating Connection.

step.cmd: To complete the connection, right-click it and select ActionConnect.
step.stepresult: This establishes communication from Node 2 to Node 1.

step.cmd: To go back to Node 1 and verify the connection, open the ScHubPort Property Sheet and confirm that under Node Switch Node 1 has accepted the connection.
To disconnect any connection, right-click the connection and select ActionDisconnect.
To clean up Idle Accepted connections from the system after a specified time, expand Connections and set Enable Idle Cleanup to true.
step.info: The default clean-up time is 1 hour for connections in a hub function and 24 hours for connections in the node switch. You can change these default values as needed.
